record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: What is the exact relationship between projected entangled pair states and quantum cellular automata in two and higher spatial dimensions?

evidence.quote: Question 16 Which is the exact relation between PEPS and QCA in 2D and higher dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix a spatial dimension D ≥ 2 and consider a D-dimensional lattice (e.g., Z^D) with a finite-dimensional Hilbert space attached to each site.

(a) A projected entangled pair state (PEPS) on this lattice is defined as follows. To each edge incident to a site one assigns an auxiliary (virtual) Hilbert space of finite "bond dimension" D_b, and to each site one places a maximally entangled pair across each adjacent edge. A linear map (the local PEPS tensor) A: (C^{D_b})^{⊗(2D)} → C^d is then applied at every site, where d is the physical dimension; the resulting global pure state on the physical lattice is the PEPS. A translation-invariant PEPS is one where the same tensor A is used at every site.

(b) A quantum cellular automaton (QCA) on the same lattice is a *-automorphism α of the quasi-local C*-algebra of observables that is translation-invariant and strictly local, in the sense that there exists a finite radius r such that for every site x, α maps observables supported at x into observables supported in the ball of radius r about x. Two QCAs are considered equivalent if they differ by a finite-depth circuit of local unitaries (and ancilla stabilization).

Problem. Determine the precise mathematical relationship between the class of translation-invariant PEPS (parametrized by their local tensors and bond dimensions) and the class of QCAs in dimension D ≥ 2. Specifically:

(i) Characterize which QCAs α can be obtained as the action that maps the trivial product state to a (translation-invariant) PEPS, or equivalently arise as the entangling isometry/unitary implicit in a PEPS construction.

(ii) Conversely, characterize which translation-invariant PEPS arise from applying a QCA to a product state, and relate the bond dimension and tensor structure of the PEPS to the locality radius and equivalence class of the QCA.

(iii) Identify obstructions (such as nontrivial QCA index/invariants in D ≥ 2 and the existence of nontrivial QCAs in D = 3) that prevent a one-to-one correspondence, and provide an exact dictionary between PEPS and QCA in D ≥ 2.
artifact.category_tag: Tensor networks and quantum cellular automata
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2020–2023) explores partial connections between stabilizer/Clifford PEPS and QCA in 2D, and establishes the existence of nontrivial QCAs in 3D (Haah–Fidkowski–Hastings), but no exact general dictionary between PEPS and QCA in dimensions D ≥ 2 has been established. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nontrivial Quantum Cellular Automata in Higher Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of nontrivial QCAs in 3D not equivalent to finite-depth circuits, indicating richer QCA structure beyond 2D classification.
status_evidence.claim: Higher-dimensional QCA classification is not complete, complicating any exact PEPS-QCA correspondence.

status_evidence.title: Classification of measurement-based quantum wire in stabilizer PEPS
status_evidence.snippet: Stabilizer PEPS transmission behaviors fall into 13 classes, one corresponding to Clifford QCAs.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial relationships between special PEPS subclasses and QCAs are known.
